This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/automation.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/automation.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `08d3b7996a7c4fbb18d52715131f5a8e490b05b3` — the merge of head `f079e341ff364bdac211e75e39f9950987007303` into base `17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 08d3b7996a7c4fbb18d52715131f5a8e490b05b3 && git checkout 08d3b7996a7c4fbb18d52715131f5a8e490b05b3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c f079e341ff364bdac211e75e39f9950987007303 && git checkout -B drift-repro 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c && git merge --no-ff f079e341ff364bdac211e75e39f9950987007303

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 17ed9e7bfd65532d83109273837e4a44624dee5c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cwxJaQdC11ABGtTez8

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `f079e341ff364bdac211e75e39f9950987007303` (Fixes #35357: an approval escalation can count `timeoutHours` as working time on an organization calendar). It delivers the card. No blocker. Four notes below, none owed before landing.

**Gates on this head:** `l1-face --pr 35929` CLEAN (13 items, none flagged). Check-runs at f079e341: 63 success, 11 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` both success. Dogfood battery not owed (no `!`, no narrowing). `check-governed-merges`: not governed, so a4-W lands.

**The card's Done-when, checked against the code and my own runs:**
- **Friday 17:00 + 4 hours fires on the next working day, across a holiday and a 调休 Saturday.** `approval-service-sla-calendar-clock.test.ts` runs on the real `WorkCalendarService` (objectql), not a copy. I ran it here: 12 passed. Positive control: I replaced the working-time branch of `slaDeadline` with the wall-clock answer, and 6 of 12 went red (the six `working_time` cases). Restored, 12 green. That matches the dev's ablation.
- **A calendar that can't answer does not escalate, and the read says why.** `runEscalations` counts a refusal and `continue`s before the single-shot check, so nothing escalates. The next sweep asks again, because refusals are never cached (`work-calendar-service.ts` drops a rejected entry). The read serves `sla_due_refusal` in place of `sla_due_at`. All three read paths project it: the open answer (`openNodeRequest`), the list read and `getRequest`. `rowFromRequest` has no other caller.
- **`wall_clock` unchanged.** `slaDueAt` is the same arithmetic. A stored snapshot with no `clock` stays on the wall clock (`escalationCountsWorkingTime` reads only an explicit `'working_time'`). The four existing wall-clock pins pass unchanged.
- **No silent fallback (D2).** With `working_time`, `slaDueAt` answers `undefined` and the only other path is the calendar. A kernel with no calendar service is refused, never answered.
- **The plugin wiring, end to end.** I booted a real `ObjectKernel` with `ObjectQLPlugin`, a SQLite `SqlDriver`, the two platform calendar objects and `ApprovalsServicePlugin`, and inserted one default calendar. Through the `approvals` service, `slaDeadline` returned Monday 12:00 (+08:00) for Friday 17:00 + 4 hours. A named code that doesn't exist returned the `not_found` refusal with its message. So `ctx.getService(WORK_CALENDAR_SERVICE)` resolves lazily and the SQL reads go through. (A third probe, for another organization, read the first one's calendar. That kernel had no SecurityPlugin to scope `{ isSystem, tenantId }` reads, so this says nothing about this PR. Organization scoping is the calendar service's, from #35355.) It was a temporary file and has been deleted.
- **Lint (static only, D9).** `approval-escalation-calendar-without-working-time` fires on a calendar beside no clock and beside `wall_clock`. Nothing checks that the calendar exists. I ran it: 66 passed. Positive control: with the rule switched off, its test went red (1 failed). Restored.

**Scope and declarations:**
- `Fixes` is right: spec keys, sweep, read projection, the cannot-answer path, lint, Studio fields, inbox reason and docs are all here. The skills text goes to the `Skills-docs:` follow-up.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #35931` is true. `skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md:350` still says "the platform ships no business-hours calendar", which this round makes false. #35931 (domain:skills, p1, pm:blocked on this PR) names exactly that row. Under the skills lane rule that is the right route.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` fit: two new optional keys with a wall-clock default, plus one additive served field.
- The changeset covers all five published packages touched. The spec authorable-surface and defaults ledgers each gain the keys, and the ADR anchor file is new.

**Sentence-by-sentence reads (changeset, `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`, the generated reference):**
- Changeset: every open request keeps its deadline (true: no `clock` in a stored snapshot means the wall clock). Friday 17:00 + 4 hours on 09-12 and 13-18 periods escalates at 12:00 on the next working day (true, tested). `calendar` left out means the organization default, with no wall-clock fallback (true). One function for sweep and read, never stored, a later holiday moves the deadline, a fired escalation stays fired (true: one `slaDeadline`, and single-shot is untouched). Refusal cases and the new field (true, though it also carries `calendar`). The inbox in every console language (true: 11 packs, and `ls ui/packages/i18n/src/locales` shows 11). The lint and the Studio sentences (true).
- `approvals.mdx`: the two clock bullets, "Monday, or Tuesday when Monday is a holiday, or the Saturday itself when it is a make-up workday" (all three are the test's cases), the example block (it parses: `clock`, `calendar` and `escalateTo` are all declared), the refusal paragraph and the publish sentence all hold.
- The reference page is the generated output of the new describe text. CI's generated-artifacts check is green.
- The `timeoutHours` describe text and code comment no longer say there is no calendar. The only other place on the head that still says it is ADR-0157's own context section, which is history and correct as written.

**Notes (not owed; a4-W's call whether to fold any in or file them):**
- **N1. A non-refusal calendar error fails the whole inbox list read.** `slaDeadline` rethrows anything that isn't a calendar refusal. The sweep catches it per row, but `projectWorkingTimeDue` in the list read does not. So one failed calendar read (a database error, say) turns the whole approvals list into an error, not just that row. A per-row guard in the projection that leaves `sla_due_at` absent and logs a warning would keep the inbox up.
- **N2. With no calendar service, the reason reads `no_default`.** The inbox then tells the admin "no default calendar" even when one exists. objectql always registers the service, so this only shows in a trimmed kernel. Wording only.
- **N3. The calendar field does not follow the escalation switch.** `controllerAdmits` reads only the direct controller and does not chain. With `escalation.enabled: false` and `clock: 'working_time'` stored, the clock is shown as retained and inactive, but the calendar shows as a live field. The `SIBLING_GATES` comment says "the calendar follows the switch through it", which overstates this. It's harmless, because nothing reads the calendar while escalation is off. I read this from the code and did not run it.
- **N4. One acceptance-note sentence in the PR body is off.** "A refused deadline is read once per row per read and sweep through the service's 60-second cache": refusals are never cached, so each refused row queries the calendar tables again on every inbox read. That's cheap at today's sizes, but the sentence should not say "cache".

**Landing:** not governed and not a narrowing. The seat's contract read comes next, as a4-W said, and then a4-W lands.

Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/automation.json, packages/spec/authorable-defaults/automation.json, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-approvals__src__approval-service.ts.json, ui/apps/console/src/services/approvalsApi.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/system/ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service-sla-calendar-clock.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.test.ts

PR #35929 (`Fixes #35357`), reviewed 2026-11-20T22:53Z by an isolated sub-agent of the seat. Inputs: card #35357 with its three comments (claim 7045483788, dev report 7048691545), ADR-0157 (D2, D4, D5, D8, D9, D12 and open implementation point 4), the PR body and its two comments (L1-a ACCEPT 7052291078 with four notes), the net diff against `main` `170ca481` (merge base `753091ee`, 35 files, +875 −48), and the check-runs on the head: 78 runs, 65 success, 13 skipped, none red, none pending. GitHub reports the head mergeable and clean. Nothing was built or run. Code outside the diff was read on the PR head and on `main`, not reviewed.

**Tier.** The committed tree changes two published schema files under `packages/spec/src/**`, so the face is the schema face and the tier owed is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The `Clause-②: yes` line alone would owe `TIER_DEFAULT`; one schema path in a mixed diff takes the higher tier. `check-governed-merges --pr 35929` reads 0 of 35 paths governed, so no governed tier applies.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Seven nits are listed under ④; none of them asks for a change on this head.

**The narrowing question, answered first: this is not a narrowing.** The new lint error refuses nothing that `main` accepts. Evidence is the second bullet of ①.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Authoring accept set, `ApprovalEscalationSchema`.** Two optional keys are added: `clock` (`wall_clock` or `working_time`, default `wall_clock`) and `calendar` (a string matching `WORK_CALENDAR_CODE_PATTERN`). RIGHT, and a widening. No key is removed, no value is refused, no requirement is tightened; `timeoutHours` keeps `z.number().min(1)`.
- **The lint error `approval-escalation-calendar-without-working-time` is not a narrowing.** It fires only on an approval node whose `escalation.calendar` is a non-blank string. On `main` that key cannot be in an accepted document:
  - `ApprovalEscalationSchema` is a `strictObject` on `main`, so `calendar` (and `clock`) is an unrecognized key there.
  - That refusal reaches every door that parses a flow. `FlowSchema`'s superRefine calls `flowNodeConfigRefusals`, which judges an `approval` node's config WHOLE against `ApprovalNodeConfigSchema` (`flow-node-config-refusals.ts`, the declared plugin contract map). `os validate`, `os build` and the metadata save door share that judge, `registerFlow` parses first, and the executor's own `safeParse` answers the node `success: false` (`approval-node.ts`).
  - The rule is registered `tier: 'gating'`, `input: 'parsed'` (`authoring-rules.ts`, untouched by this diff), so on `os validate`, `os build` and the save door it only sees stacks the schema accepted.
  - One door differs and I name it: `os lint` never parses, so on a raw stack (not `defineStack`) it raised nothing on `main` for such a key and raises this error now. That is the pre-flight catching up with the parse. The same stack is refused on `main` at validate, build, publish, registration and run, so it was never an accepted document.
  - Stored rows: the schema's own `history` text records that unknown keys were dropped silently before the shape was closed, and the request snapshot is a copy of the parsed config, so no stored `node_config_json` carries `clock`. `escalationCountsWorkingTime` reads only an explicit `'working_time'`.
  So the set "accepted on `main`, refused on this head" is empty. No `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` record is owed, and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` stands.
- **Parsed output.** A parsed escalation now carries `clock: 'wall_clock'` when the author wrote none, and new request snapshots store it. The output type `ApprovalEscalationParsed` gains a required `clock`; the input type gains two optional keys. The sweep and the read treat the materialized default exactly as an absent key. RIGHT.
- **Served surface, `ApprovalRequestRow`.** One optional field is added, `sla_due_refusal`. RIGHT, additive. The row is a TypeScript interface with no response schema in spec and no client package restates it; the console's own mirror (`approvalsApi.ts`) is updated.
- **`sla_due_at` without a calendar clock.** Byte-identical to `main`: `rowFromRequest` still calls `slaDueAt(created_at, cfg)`, the arithmetic is unchanged, and `projectWorkingTimeDue` skips every row that is not explicitly `working_time`.
- **`sla_due_at` under `working_time`.** Read in `slaDeadline`:
  - a calendar that answers: `addWorkingHours` from `created_at`, in the request row's own organization, on the named code or else the default;
  - a calendar that refuses (the three ledger codes, classified structurally by `isWorkCalendarRefusal`): no `sla_due_at`, and `sla_due_refusal` is served;
  - no calendar service: refused as unresolved, never a wall-clock answer;
  - no usable `timeoutHours` or `created_at`: neither field, as on the wall clock.
  `slaDueAt` returns nothing for `working_time`, and `slaDueAt`, the sweep's guard and `slaDeadline` are the only runtime readers of `timeoutHours` on the head, so no path falls back to wall-clock hours (D2). All three callers of `rowFromRequest` (the open answer, the list read, `loadRequest`) project it. Exactly one of the two fields is served, by construction.
- **`runEscalations`.** For a wall-clock row the order and the comparisons are those of `main`: the `enabled` switch with its legacy window, then the deadline, then the single-shot read. A refusal is counted and skipped before the single-shot read, so nothing escalates and no `escalate` row is written. The next sweep asks again, because the service never caches a refusal (`work-calendar-service.ts` on `main`). Nothing is stored (D12), and ADR-0042 §1 is untouched. One `warn` per sweep carries the count; that level is right under AGENTS.md's degradation rule, since the request visibly waits and its read says why.
- **Error codes.** `ERR_WORK_CALENDAR_UNRESOLVED`, `ERR_WORK_CALENDAR_NOT_MAINTAINED` and `ERR_WORK_CALENDAR_INVALID` are in `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` on `main` (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, registered by the calendar-service card). The diff mints no code. The lint rule id is a rule id, not a ledger code: like `approval-decision-outputs-reserved` it lives in the rule file and the package index only.
- **Generated mirrors.** `authorable-surface/automation.json` gains both keys, `authorable-defaults/automation.json` gains the `clock` default, the reference page is regenerated, and the ADR anchor is one new JSON file named for its path. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset` and every type-check job are green on the head.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@object-ui/console` and `@object-ui/i18n` is right. `Metadata-protocol: added` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves, and these are the published packages it moves (`@object-ui/app-shell` is private, so it takes no entry of its own). `added` is the right kind: two new authorable keys, nothing removed or tombstoned, and no existing default or meaning changed, since the wall clock is what `timeoutHours` meant before.

Both declaration lines stand line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset. No ADR-0087 marker is owed: the changeset declares nothing breaking, and `check-adr-0087-registration` judges declared-breaking changesets only. No conversion entry, tombstone or semantic entry is owed either, since no key is retired and no default flips. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right on the evidence in ①.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev report `open_questions` (one): keep the finding an `error` with its English developer message.** Answered: ACCEPT option A, as the area ruled. D9 names "a `calendar` code written without `clock: 'working_time'`" as a static authoring error the publish-time check covers. Option B (a warning, the calendar left inert) would keep a declared key that nothing reads, which ADR-0049 forbids.
- **Dev report.** `security_findings` none, `out_of_scope_findings` none. Its deviations (no assignee at PR creation, a tracking branch, `main` merged only in the fix round) have no effect on the contract.
- **ADR-0157 open implementation point 4, carried into this card's review: which organization, under whose authority.** Answered in the tree, and RIGHT. The sweep and the three reads pass the request row's own `organization_id` to the calendar service, never the caller's organization. The service reads elevated inside that organization and refuses `no_organization` outside the `single` posture when the row has none. That is the contract `work-calendar-service.ts` states on `main` ("for the approval sweep, the request's").
- **Security reading: not security-touching.** No changed hunk adds, removes or reorders a permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication check, and none teaches one. One new exposure exists and D9 rules it: a reader who can already read a request now also reads the calendar code, the date the calendar is not maintained for, and an English `message` that can carry the calendar's maintained span or the name of an unreadable column. Those come from tables a rank-and-file member cannot read directly, and always from the request's own organization. No path of this PR sits on a low-risk arm, so the template prints no machine line for it and I add none.
- **L1-a's four notes (7052291078).** Note 1 is confirmed and reaches further than stated: N1. Note 2 is confirmed: N3. Note 3 is the Studio form, the lane seat's face; I read `controllerAdmits` and agree: it reads the direct controller only and does not chain, so the `SIBLING_GATES` comment says more than the code does. Note 4 is already answered: the PR body now says a refusal is never cached and every read and sweep asks again.
- **D4 release pairing.** The body and the changeset both say the change is not released alone and name its pair. #35355 is closed; #35356 is open. Holding Version Packages until the set is complete is the maintainer's act under D4, not this PR's.
- **D12 left one choice to this card:** whether the `escalate` row records the due time it fired on. Settled as no, stated in the PR body. ACCEPT; the row's own `created_at` says when it fired.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up #35931` is true.** `skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md:350` still says the platform ships no business-hours calendar. #35931 (p1, blocked on this PR) names that row and the two neighbouring places.
- **Overlap with #35789 (open, not queued).** Its two hunks in the plugin's `approval-service.ts` sit in `ApprovalMessagingSurface` and in the channel list inside `notify`. This PR's hunks sit in the import block, `slaDueAt` and its helpers, `ApprovalServiceOptions`, the constructor, the three read projections and `runEscalations`. No shared line and no shared behaviour, so either order merges. No commit on `main` since the merge base touches the plugin, the two spec files, the lint rule or the inbox page.
- **SQL push-down.** No id materialisation and no in-app join is added. The deadline is counted in memory per row, which ADR-0157 D6 requires ("No calendar math runs in SQL"). The calendar read behind it is the service's and is cached per organization and code; N2 covers the refused case.
- **Author.** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no off-relay note is owed. The PR is still a draft; readying it is the seat's.

### ④ Design judgment
